رِيحٌ سَهُوكٌ and ↓ سَاهِكَةٌ (K) and ↓ سَيْهَكٌ and ↓ سَيْهُوكٌ (S, K) [like سَهُوجٌ and سَاهِجَةٌ &c.] A vehement, or violent, wind, (S, K, TA,) paring [the ground]; (TA;) as also ↓ مَسْهَكَةٌ : (O, K:) [pl. of ↓ the second سَوَاهِكُ:] El-Kumeyt says, “رَمَادًا أَطَارَتْهُ السَّوَاهِكُ رِمْدِدَا
” [Ashes which the violent winds made to fly away reduced to the most minute particles]. (S.) ―
-b2- السَّهُوكُ The eagle. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
